sourceCopy.name: Rational Expression Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Rational Expression Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Simplify polynomial fractions, cancel common factors and keep excluded values visible. Free local calculator, no sign-up.
sourceCopy.intro: Enter integer-coefficient polynomials in x to reduce a rational expression. The result keeps the original denominator restriction, so cancellation never hides values that make the input undefined.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: How do you simplify a rational expression?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Factor the numerator and denominator, cancel their common polynomial and retain the original denominator’s zeros as restrictions. For example, x²−1 over x−1 reduces to x+1, with x≠1 still excluded.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. Parsing and simplification run locally in this browser; inputs are not uploaded or saved.

fields.numeratorHint: Use integer coefficients and x, for example x^2-1. Powers up to 8.
fields.denominatorHint: Use integer coefficients and x, for example x-1. It cannot be zero.
fields.limitsNote: Supports one variable x, integer coefficients up to 1,000,000 and degree up to 8. No parentheses or decimal coefficients.

messages.checkInputs: Check both polynomials and the supported limits.
messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is not available in this browser.

additionalFaqs.question: Why keep a restriction after cancelling a factor?
additionalFaqs.answer: The simplified expression may be defined at a value where the original denominator was zero. That value remains excluded from the original expression’s domain.

additionalFaqs.question: What polynomial format is supported?
additionalFaqs.answer: Use a single variable x with integer coefficients, such as 2x^3−x+4. Powers from 0 to 8 are supported; parentheses, decimal coefficients and multiple variables are not.

additionalFaqs.question: Does this find every possible factorization?
additionalFaqs.answer: It cancels the exact common polynomial factor using integer arithmetic. It does not provide a complete factorization into irreducible linear or quadratic factors.
